residencyRequirements.description: Either spouse must be an Australian citizen, domiciled in Australia, or ordinarily resident in Australia for at least 12 months immediately before the application (Family Law Act 1975 (Cth), s.39(3)).

waitingPeriod.description: No waiting period after filing. Divorce Order takes effect 1 month and 1 day after made (Family Law Act 1975 (Cth), s.55).

noFault.name: Irretrievable Breakdown (12-Month Separation)
noFault.description: The marriage has broken down irretrievably, demonstrated by 12 months of continuous separation.

basic.name: Application for Divorce
basic.description: Filed in the Family Court of Western Australia under the Family Law Act 1975 (Cth) and Family Court Act 1997 (WA)

basic.name: Affidavit — Proof of Separation
basic.description: Supporting affidavit confirming the 12-month separation period

basic.name: Marriage Certificate
basic.description: Certified copy of the marriage certificate

legalCitations.description: Federal statute — sole ground for divorce (s.48)
Establishes the Family Court of Western Australia
Repealed presumption of equal shared parental responsibility (s.61DA); reformed parenting and property provisions (in force 6 May 2024)

filingFees.notes: Fee effective 1 July 2025. Reduced fee of AUD $375 available for financial hardship. Fee is the same as the federal court.

effectiveDateRule: The Divorce Order takes effect 1 month and 1 day after the order is made (Family Law Act 1975 (Cth), s.55).
certificateNote: A sealed Divorce Order can be obtained from the Family Court of Western Australia registry after the order takes effect.
specialNote: Western Australia is the only Australian state with its own Family Court (Family Court of Western Australia), established under the Family Court Act 1997 (WA). All other states use the Federal Circuit and Family Court of Australia.
